overview.title: United Nations
overview.definition: The United Nations (UN) is an international organization founded in 1945, committed to maintaining international peace and security, developing friendly relations among nations, and promoting social progress, better living standards, and human rights.
overview.importanceInUpsc: Crucial for GS Paper II (International Relations, Global Groupings, UN Organs, Reforms) and Prelims (factual questions on UN agencies, specialized bodies, headquarters, and resolutions).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of United Nations.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Core foundational concepts of International Relations

sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **UN Charter**: Signed on 26 June 1945, serving as the foundational treaty of the international organization; it codifies the major principles of international relations from sovereign equality to prohibition of the use of force.
• **Principal Organs**: Consists of six primary organs: **General Assembly (UNGA)**, **Security Council (UNSC)**, **Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC)**, **Trusteeship Council** (operation suspended in 1994), **International Court of Justice (ICJ)**, and the **Secretariat**.
• **Headquarters**: Located in **New York City**, with major offices in Geneva, Vienna, and Nairobi, endowing it with international territory status.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Financed by assessed and voluntary contributions from member states, with the **United States** being the largest contributor followed by China and Japan.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: UNGA (universal representation), UNSC (15 members, 5 P5 with veto), ICJ (The Hague, judicial organ).
Chapter IV & V of UN Charter
High frequency of direct Prelims statements regarding voting powers and composition.
Autonomous organizations linked to the UN through negotiated agreements (e.g., WHO, ILO, FAO, UNESCO).
Often tested via headquarters location, formation year, or flagship reports.
Subsidiary organs of the UN General Assembly focusing on specific developmental or humanitarian mandates (e.g., UNICEF, UNDP, UNEP).
Created by UNGA resolutions under Article 22
Direct links to international developmental indices and global funding mechanisms.

items.definition: The power of the five permanent members of the UNSC (China, France, Russia, UK, USA) to block any substantive resolution; a negative vote by any P5 member defeats the resolution.
Resolution 377 (V) adopted in 1950 stating that in any case where the UNSC fails to act due to a lack of unanimity of the permanent members, the UNGA may consider the matter immediately.

items.term: Specialized Agencies vs. Funds and Programmes
items.definition: Specialized agencies are legally independent international organizations with their own membership and budgets, whereas funds and programmes are organs directly created by the UNGA and depend entirely on voluntary contributions.
G4 Nations (India, Brazil, Germany, Japan) seeking permanent seats in an expanded UNSC; L.69 Group advocating for comprehensive UNSC reform.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Region / Zone Details**: Global operations coordinated through four primary headquarters: New York (Americas), Geneva (Europe/Human Rights), Vienna (Narcotics/Outer Space/Atomic Energy), and Nairobi (Environment/UNEP).
• **Driving Advantages**: Ensures decentralized global representation, regional crisis monitoring, and localized execution of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Anachronistic UNSC structure reflecting 1945 power dynamics, financial crises due to delayed contributions, geopolitical polarization limiting peacekeeping effectiveness.
• **Policy Interventions**: Intergovernmental Negotiations (IGN) framework, advocacy for transparent selection of Secretary-General, strengthening multilateralism through 'Our Common Agenda' report.

items.title: Mnemonic for P5 Permanent Members
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: **FREBC** (or **FRUCS**: France, Russia, USA, China, UK).
• **Decoded Meaning**: France, Russia, United Kingdom, China, United States.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly distinguishes P5 members from elected non-permanent members in multi-statement questions.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Remember that ICJ is the *only* principal organ not located in New York; its seat is at the Peace Palace in **The Hague, Netherlands**.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently creates confusion by stating that the International Criminal Court (ICC) is a principal judicial organ of the UN. In reality, the ICC is an independent international judicial body and not a UN agency, whereas the ICJ is the principal judicial organ of the UN.

Mains Value Addition: Emphasize 'Effective Multilateralism' and quote the Secretary-General's 'Our Common Agenda' report. Mention India's principled stance on reformed multilateralism (Nairobi Declaration, G4 aspirations) for scoring high marks in GS Paper II.

keyTakeaways: The UN architecture comprises six principal organs, with specialized agencies operating as legally independent entities.
UNSC reform remains a contentious global debate centered around the P5 veto, equitable regional representation, and the G4 framework.
Distinguishing between specialized agencies (independent budget) and UN funds/programmes (voluntary contributions) is critical for Prelims elimination.
